title: voices-accelerant-catalog-and-priority-ledgers-sep-2027
content:
Purpose:
A compact synthesis of recent customer feedback (Aug 2027) focused on runtime correctness, cost-performance trade-offs, and small feature asks that unblock pilots. Aim is to surface high-leverage microfeatures and low-effort engineering patches that improve retention for mid-market and enterprise customers.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Six recurrent pain threads: latency tail spikes, hallucination/structured-output regressions, embedding drift across model upgrades, KV-cache eviction surprises, capacity-commitment friction on Dedicated, and opacity in per-route cost attribution.
- Quick wins (2–6 wks): per-route ephemeral caching toggle, lightweight token-cost attribution header, a deterministic fallback policy for short-lived tail spikes, and a ‘sample-output’ schema validator. Estimated combined engineering effort: 3–6 sprint-weeks if parallelized.
- Medium projects (6–12 wks): per-customer embedding-anchoring option (automated recalibration), dedicated autoscale predictor UI, and rollout telemetry hook for structured-output regressions.
- Suggested next step: run two small pilots (one mid-market SaaS customer and one regulated enterprise) with the quick-wins set to measure churn risk delta over 8 weeks.

Top six themes (annotated):
1) Latency tail spikes (impact: High, freq: High)
- What customers say: "90th–99th latency kills our UX during traffic bursts; sometimes responses time out while others succeed."
- Root signals: bursts from long-form generations + occasional colocation GC on GPU nodes + upstream retry patterns.
- Short patch: add a deterministic fallback routing policy that proxies overflow short requests to a low-latency compatible variant (alpha: small LLM, lower cost) when queue depth > threshold. (Owner: eng-serving-runtime; ticket: JIRA-CS-3492)
- Metric to watch: 95/99 p50 gap and percent of requests rerouted.

2) Structured-output regressions & hallucinations (impact: High, freq: Medium)
- Customers using tool-calling/JSON responses report subtle schema breaks after model bumps.
- Short patch: introduce a sampling-based schema validator (server-side) with optional auto-reject or soft-warning. Allows product teams to flag regressions before rollout. (Owner: product-hosted-api + applied-ml; ticket: JIRA-PR-4120)

3) Embedding drift across model upgrades (impact: Medium, freq: Medium)
- Several customers noted search and similarity quality drops after we switched embedding variants for a catalog model.
- Medium fix: per-customer embedding anchoring — allow pinning of an embedding model + automated reindex sampling to estimate QA delta pre-rollout. (Owner: product-optimize; linked: CON-emb-anchors)

4) KV-cache eviction/pinning surprises (impact: Medium, freq: Low–Medium)
- Enterprise customers with bursty conversational patterns lose cached context unexpectedly when route hop occurs or when autoscaling evicts a node. This increases tokens and latencies.
- Short patch: provide an ephemeral KV pinning API that marks sessions as ‘sticky’ for a bounded TTL (configurable). (Owner: serving-runtime; ticket: JIRA-RUNTIME-581)

5) Dedicated capacity and commit friction (impact: High for some, freq: Low)
- Procurement/finance complaints: rough forecasting for commit tiers; inability to easily test burst policies without long-term commit.
- Medium/long project: build a sandboxed dedicated burst demo environment & an API for short-term elevates (7–14 day reserved bursts with prorated pricing) to reduce sales friction. (Owner: dedicated; sales ops)

6) Per-route cost opacity (impact: Medium, freq: High)
- Customers want finer token/unit attribution by route, model variant, and prefix. Some have built their own instrumentation since platform granularity is coarse.
- Quick patch: emit a token-attribution header and a per-invocation trace ID that feeds to Console as a lightweight report. (Owner: observability; ticket: JIRA-OBS-224)

Microfeature request catalogue (short descriptions + effort estimate):
- per-route ephemeral caching toggle (quick, 1–2 wks) 
- token-cost attribution header + CSV export (quick, 2–3 wks)
- sample-output schema validator + soft-fail mode (quick, 3–4 wks)
- session stickiness API for KV cache (quick/medium, 3–5 wks)
- per-customer embedding anchoring and pre-rollout QA (medium, 6–8 wks)
- short-reserved-burst product for Dedicated (medium, 8–12 wks)
- per-rollout structured-output regression alert (medium, 6–10 wks)

Customer vignettes (representative, anonymized):
- AdRevenueCo (mid-market): Noticed 15% drop in retrieval precision after embedding swap; flagged by internal QA tests. Would accept a rollback window or preflight anchor to avoid production regressions.
- HealthVault (regulated enterprise): Needs deterministic evidence that a model fallback did not produce PHI leakage; requests logs + schema validation with proof of non-hallucination for audit trails.
- ChatDocs (scale-up startup): Sees tail latency during end-of-day batch exports; prefers a stickiness TTL for conversational sessions to retain KV cache across short autoscale events.

Risk/impact assessment matrix (qualitative):
- Quick patches: low-to-medium engineering risk; high customer-perceived ROI.
- Medium projects: medium engineering risk; higher infra/ops coordination and compliance checks.

Proposed prioritization (recommended):
1) token-cost header + console CSV export (low lift, immediate transparency)
2) sample-output schema validator (reduces major regression risk for structured outputs)
3) session stickiness TTL for KV cache (reduces token cost and latencies for bursty customers)
4) embedding anchoring pilot (measure retrieval delta pre/post)

Proposed pilot plan (8 weeks):
- Week 0: lock down quick patches and select pilot customers (AdRevenueCo + ChatDocs).
- Weeks 1–2: deploy token header + schema validator in soft-warning mode; collect telemetry.
- Weeks 3–6: enable KV pinning TTL for pilot customers and monitor token usage, latency, and retrieval quality.
- Week 7: evaluate metrics, customer satisfaction signals, and decide whether to hard-gate schema validation for rollouts.
- Week 8: decision meeting with eng/product/CS. (Owner: Aisha Malik + Jonah Peters)

Measurement plan (signals to capture):
- 95/99 latency percentiles (pre/post)
- per-route token delta and cost delta (CSV)
- retrieval precision/recall on a small canonical set for embedding pilots
- schema validation hit-rate and false-positive rate
- customer NPS/CSAT delta and pilot retention intention

Raw quote appendix (anonymized):
- "We lost the search quality overnight after the embedding switch — we have to roll back or face unhappy users." — AdRevenueCo eng lead
- "We need to show auditors that a fallback didn't invent a diagnosis; otherwise we can't certify this workflow." — HealthVault security
- "If the session cache drops mid-conversation, our token bills spike and users see weird duplicated replies." — ChatDocs product manager

Open questions / decisions required:
- Do we default the schema-validator to soft-warning or to hard-block for structured outputs? (Tradeoff: developer velocity vs safety)
- What SLA/price for short-reserved bursts would be acceptable to sales/legal? Need market input.

Suggested immediate actions (this week):
- CS: reach out to AdRevenueCo + ChatDocs for explicit permission to run the 8-week pilot (Aisha).
- Product: scope minimal schema-validator endpoint and define JSON schema config format (Jonah).
- Eng (serving-runtime): spike the session stickiness API and return mock telemetry (Rosa).
- Observability: create a Console report skeleton for token-cost CSV (Diego).

Notes & references:
- Related Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/CS/voices-accelerant-2027
- Suggested tickets: JIRA-CS-3492, JIRA-OBS-224, JIRA-RUNTIME-581, JIRA-PR-4120
- Slack thread for pilot coordination: #cs-runtime-threads

End of doc.

Author notes: This draft intentionally mixes polished synth + quick internal playbook language to be actionable for eng/product/CS. Please annotate with additional customer names or missing micro-asks; we'll fold into a follow-up decision memo if pilots are greenlit.
